text:
ryan: quick thread, ran a multi-model co-residency sim on a single A100 (3 models: small-chat, med-code, med-embed). saw unexpected OOM/degeneration with slab_reuse enabled.
sara: can you paste the config you used?
ryan: config: ```
serving.co_residency: true
allocator.strategy: slab_reuse
allocator.workspace_mb: 512
swap.policy: predictive_prefetch
kv_cache.mode: per_request_shared
batching.dynamic_threshold: 8
```
devin: interesting — predictive_prefetch + slab reuse can race with KV cache growth. what did profiler show for workspace spikes?
ryan: peak workspace 5GB when med-code got a long seq (1024) even though pinned workspace_mb 512. looks like transient growth from transient tensor allocations + kernel workspace.
ryan: profiler excerpt: ```
[profiler] t=0.42s model=med-code kernel_selection: matmul_fused_fast (0.78), aten_mm (0.15), custom_attention (0.07)
[profiler] kv_cache.size pre/ post request: 1.2G -> 2.9G
[profiler] slab.evictions: 42, reuse_hits: 210, alloc_fallbacks: 6
```
olivia: wait, kv_cache jumped by 1.7G during a single request? that shouldn't happen if shared prefix cache is working.
ryan: yeah looks like per-request growth because embedding model warmed new prefixes, not shared correctly across co-resident models.
sara: do you have timeline showing which model triggered the growth?
ryan: timeline: small-chat (burst) -> med-embed request triggers cold KV cache build -> med-code long seq arrives -> workspace + kv spikes -> OOM in slab allocator for med-code -> swap kicked in but too late.
devin: so eviction policy currently prioritizes LRU within slab, but cross-model fairness is missing. When co-resident models compete, larger KV growth can steal slabs. We probably need per-model reservation + soft limit + preemptive shrink.
sara: Agreed. Options: 1) per-model min-reserve (e.g., 1GB), 2) adaptive workspace shrink on long-tail kernels, 3) prefetch throttling for KV cache building, 4) move some KV to host pinned memory earlier (async swap).
olivia: Also check kernel selection — matmul_fused_fast uses extra temporary workspace; if we force aten_mm for med-code on long sequences it might reduce workspace at expense of compute time but avoid OOM. We can route by sequence length.
devin: propose heuristic: if seq_len > 512 and predicted_kv_growth + kernel_workspace > free_slab_budget -> switch to low-workspace kernel and enable kv-paging for that request.
ryan: did a quick experiment: forced low-workspace kernel for med-code long seqs, p99 latency went +18% but OOMs dropped to zero and cost per token only +12%. For production, tradeoff might be acceptable.
sara: can we auto-evaluate effect on throughput? Batch simulator?
ryan: ran micro-sim with synthetic arrival distribution: concurrency=12, mix = [0.6 small-chat, 0.2 med-embed, 0.2 med-code]. results: baseline slab_reuse + predictive_prefetch -> 3 OOMs / hr; with kernel-fallback + kv-prefetch-throttle -> 0 OOMs / hr, avg latency +6%.
ryan: sample sim log: ```
SIM: concurrency=12 mix=[.6,.2,.2]
BASE: oom=3 latency_mean=120ms p99=410ms
PATCH: oom=0 latency_mean=127ms p99=484ms
RESOURCE: gpu_mem_total=40G free_avg=4.1G
```
olivia: sounds promising. but the root cause is allocator granularity — slab chunk size too big for mixed workloads. smaller slab chunks reduce internal fragmentation.
devin: true, but smaller chunks increase metadata overhead and fragmentation management cost. we should try hybrid: two slab classes (large_chunks for model weights, small_chunks for temporaries/KV). also add cross-model accounting to avoid one model consuming all small_chunks.
sara: also want to try pre-reserving ephemeral workspace per-request based on predicted kernel path. add a reservation cache: predict workspace_need(seq_len, model, kernel) -> reserve N bytes ahead of allocation. If reservation fails, fall back early.
ryan: here's a quick pseudo-rule we tested: ```
if predict_kv_growth(model, req) + predict_kernel_ws(seq_len, model) > free_budget * 0.6:
    switch_kernel = True
    throttle_kv_prefetch = True
    reserve_host_swap = True
```
olivia: do we have a reliable predictor for kv growth? the embedding model builds KV based on unique tokens and role tokens; we can use a running estimator (exponential moving avg) of prefix growth per model type.
devin: implement simple estimator first, then swap to ML predictor later. also add a safe-evict call: preemptively evict least-recently-used non-pinned KV shards when a new large request is admitted.
sara: next steps: (1) add per-model min-reserve and two slab classes (2) implement kernel-fallback by seq_len routing (3) kv prefetch throttling + estimator (4) re-run sim and real-capture traces. assign: devin for allocator changes, olivia for kernel-routing, ryan for sim & traces, sara to coordinate and write RFC.
ci-bot: deploy scheduled: allocator-branch -> perf-test staging at 2026-03-19T09:00Z :rocket:
sara: good. also add unit that records 'evicted_by_model' tag to slab events so we can see cross-model eviction patterns in traces.
ryan: will attach the raw trace in follow-up message. short-term patch seems safe: kernel-fallback + kv throttle. thanks team :thumbsup:
